commits.edited_message:
Reject invalid CENC IV metadata before decryption

Validate key records and IV sizes before configuring the decrypter. Check multikey SAI indices against the current declared key count so key-info changes cannot expose undeclared trailing records.

Size the PIFF track-encryption box to its stored key record — algorithm id, IV size and KID — instead of the aligned in-memory object.

Keep the shared validator available without ISO media support and add regression coverage for valid and malformed IV metadata.

Fix PIFF default key-info size

The PIFF default-info getter reports 19 bytes for a 20-byte key record. This truncates the advertised KID and causes CENC validation to reject valid PIFF streams.

Return the key-info array's size. When the per-sample IV size is zero, count the constant-IV size byte that follows the KID, as the tenc default-info length does.

Add a regression test that creates PIFF protection through the public API and checks the returned size, record contents, and validation.

Verify valid PIFF playback, unchanged PIFF+CENC decryption output, and all 13 existing CLI reproduction cases.

coupling: The overflowing read is not in either edited diff. gf_cenc_validate_key_info, moved unchanged by 37599b9, reads the constant-IV size at the first byte after a parsed single-key record once key_info_size reaches that index. 37599b9 allocates the PIFF tenc box to offsetof(key_info)+20, the stored algorithm/IV/KID record, instead of sizeof(GF_PIFFTrackEncryptionBox), which drops the 4-byte alignment tail after the array. Every access that commit still performs stays inside those 20 bytes, and the unedited f214065 getter reports exactly 20, so a zero per-sample IV is rejected before the following byte is touched. f214065 still returns sizeof(key_info) for the 8- and 16-byte IV sizes its regression test covers; when the per-sample IV size is 0 it counts one extra byte, the constant-IV size the tenc getter already accounts for. On a sizeof allocation that byte sits in the alignment tail, so the validator read does not fault. key_info[20] is therefore inside the historical object and one byte past the record-sized object, and the length is 21 only after f214065. Replaying either edited commit alone leaves this input clean. A correct fix has to reconcile the two contracts because the failing access is in neither hunk. Changing only the allocation diff leaves f214065 reporting a length the record-sized box does not contain; changing only the length diff leaves 37599b9's record-sized box in place for any caller that still counts the constant-IV byte. The overflow is the composition, so neither diff can be repaired in isolation without the other commit's contract.
